accepted_claims: track_components requires sampled_frames keyword-only, with no default and a non-optional annotation; omission is a TypeError and explicit None is a ValueError.

No supported call in the permitted stack reaches the tracker without an explicit declared schedule; no alias, default, reconstructed unit cadence or schedule-position fallback remains; each transition's right frame derives from the declared schedule.

Publishing COMPLETE and returning analysis access both require the lifecycle contract to have been executed, canonically persisted, re-read from disk and independently reverified; in-memory evidence is discarded.
All twelve completion-manifest fields are tamper-covered: altering any one denies analysis access.

An empty right detector frame representing disappearance at declared non-unit cadence is retained as terminal information and does not cause global rejection; exactly-one-terminal accounting holds end to end, including the required full example at schedule (0, 5, 11, 12).

Every schedule perturbation that removes or displaces an OCCUPIED frame, or inserts a frame into a live interval, blocks COMPLETE and writes nothing: reordering, truncation that drops an occupied frame, interior insertion inside a live interval, interior and horizon value substitution, and the empty schedule. Perturbations OUTSIDE occupied frames and live intervals are NOT blocked - see limitation L1.
All 13 mandatory historical mutants are killed, each by at least one semantic killer that is not a hash tripwire.

limitations.title: The declared schedule is bound only on occupied frames and live intervals; elsewhere it is free in BOTH directions
limitations.found_by: Reviewer A (blocker B1 at round 1, blocker B2 at round 2); refined by Reviewer B (O1, O8)
measured_rule: let OCCUPIED = every track-point frame union every event frame
(i) the schedule must be non-empty, strictly increasing, non-negative integers

(iii) it must contain no frame OTHER THAN THAT TRACK'S OWN POINT FRAMES strictly inside any track's point span, and none strictly between a track's last point and that track's terminal-event frame [wording precision requested by Reviewer A, round 3 minor 1: read without that clause the rule would contradict clause (ii) for any track with three or more points]
(iii) it must contain no frame strictly inside any track's point span, and none strictly between a track's last point and that track's terminal-event frame
(iv) if some track's last point sits at the tracker's final frame the declared last entry must equal it; OTHERWISE THE TAIL IS FREE, both to extend arbitrarily and to truncate
limitations.statement: future_lifecycle_runner does not invoke track_components, so it cannot know how many samples were taken nor where the run truly ended. Outside occupied frames and live intervals the declared schedule may be extended by any number of frames, and an unoccupied trailing frame may be deleted. A three-sample run can be published as ending 1,000,000 frames later. Prefix extension is available to every run that does not begin at frame 0.
superseded_claims: round 0: 'the residual is a single position that is empty and event-free' - FALSIFIED by Reviewer A B1

round 1: 'extension anywhere with no point or event, monotonicity holding and the horizon preserved' - FALSIFIED by Reviewer A B2 in both directions: the horizon is not preserved in general, truncation is also possible, prefix extension is available to occupied runs, and an unoccupied inserted frame is still refused inside a live interval
limitations.pinned_by: test_rs01_09a (every occupied frame refuses divergence), test_rs01_09b (all six measured cases), test_rs01_09c (zero-track)
limitations.disposition: FUTURE_REAL_RUNNER_OBLIGATION: a real runner must hand ONE schedule object to both the tracker and the publisher.

limitations.title: Zero-track runs carry no schedule binding
limitations.statement: A run in which nothing was ever detected has no occupancy anywhere, so clauses (ii)-(iv) of the measured rule are vacuous and the schedule's CONTENT is unconstrained: COMPLETE publishes against an entirely unrelated schedule. The well-formedness floor (i) still holds - an empty schedule and negative frames are refused (Reviewer B, m2), so 'wholly unconstrained' would overstate it.

limitations.title: A Mapping is accepted as a schedule at the runner boundary
limitations.statement: track_components refuses a Mapping (ordered-sequence-only, pinned by test_12e); the runner performs no such type check, so a dict with increasing key order publishes. No false evidence results because the keys are the true schedule.
limitations.disposition: NOT_REPAIRED: repair would require a production-source change, which the protocol reserves for load-bearing failures.

limitations.title: A one-shot iterator schedule leaves an orphan lifecycle document
limitations.statement: The runner consumes the schedule twice. A generator is exhausted by the first pass, so publication is refused after the lifecycle document has already been written. Fail-closed is preserved: the orphan alone never unlocks analysis and it blocks retry.

limitations.title: Redundant limbs in the defensive publication layer are not individually pinned
limitations.found_by: Reviewer B (M5 at round 1, m1 at round 2)
limitations.statement: At least six mutants inside _publish_new_canonical_file die only to hash tripwires: the three post-link identity limbs, the target_linked cleanup, os.fsync, and sort_keys. Reviewer B found three more in round 2 - the mkstemp prefix, the '.partial' suffix, and follow_symlinks=False on the ownership stat - so this list is NON-EXHAUSTIVE for that region. The limbs are pairwise redundant against the existing tests, so no test isolates any one of them. The module docstring promises a leftover is named '.<target>.<random>.partial'; no test pins that naming. Fail-closed behaviour is unaffected.

limitations.title: Content-addressed, not provenance-bound
limitations.statement: Copying a genuine LIFECYCLE.json + COMPLETION.json pair into another directory yields access there. This is stated verbatim in the runner module docstring and is not a new finding.
